script: My dad exposed a hidden secret about Lolita that shattered my world.. I was eight, maybe nine, rocking a pair of cheap rectangular sunglasses I'd snatched off a curb, thinking I was the coolest kid in the block. My dad saw me strutting around with them and went all "you're a dork, those are like the ones Lolita wore, people are going to think…." (micro‑hook: "Dad's face turned to a comic book villain.") "Lolita?" I asked, my voice a mix of curiosity and annoyance. He launched into a monologue about a teenage seductress who'd "seduced middle‑aged men." (micro‑hook: "Dad's version of Lolita had a face‑palm moment.") Later, I Googled her. Turns out she's a 12‑year‑old victim of a stalker, not a femme fatale. My dad was on a whole other level of clueless. I felt the sting of his ignorance and the absurdity of his warning. I mean, who even knows about that? (I know exactly what he was on.) I laughed, then got mad. I'd never been so annoyed by a dad's over‑analysis. The internet? Oh, you're welcome for the tea.
